title: A T. rex named Gus just sold for $50 million — and it's as long as a school bus!
summary:
Imagine digging in the dirt on a ranch and finding the toe bone of a Tyrannosaurus rex! That's what happened to a fossil-hunting team in South Dakota in 2021. They were just about to leave when they decided to check one more spot. Within hours, they found a toe bone. It turned out to be part of a huge T. rex skeleton they named Gus, after the ranch owner who passed away during the dig.

Now, Gus has sold for a jaw-dropping $50.1 million at an auction in New York. That's more money than most people will ever see! The bidding war lasted only 10 minutes, but the price shot way past the $20 to $30 million experts expected. It even beat the old record for a dinosaur fossil, which was $44.6 million for a Stegosaurus named Apex in 2024.

Gus is one of the biggest and most complete T. rex skeletons ever found. It stands 12.5 feet tall and stretches 38 feet long — about as long as a school bus! It has 183 bones, which is about 61% of a full T. rex skeleton. Its skull is so heavy that the auction house had to use a fake one on the display. The real skull sat in its own special case.

But here's the coolest part: Gus has 30 of its 32 belly ribs, called gastralia. Those thin, fragile bones hardly ever survive as fossils. Gus also has healed bite marks from another tyrannosaur, showing it had some tough fights millions of years ago.

Nobody knows who bought Gus because the buyer wants to stay secret. Scientists are a little worried. If rich people buy more fossils, they might end up in private collections where nobody can study them. But some buyers have loaned their dinosaurs to museums before, so there's hope Gus will still be seen by kids like you!
why_it_matters: If fossils like Gus disappear into private homes, kids may lose the chance to see them in museums and learn about dinosaurs.

background_read: Tyrannosaurus rex was one of the largest meat-eating dinosaurs; its name means 'tyrant lizard king.'
South Dakota (a state in the middle of the United States) is known as a rich place for dinosaur fossils.
Complete dinosaur skeletons are rare, so each new find helps scientists learn more.

WHERE: The fossil was found in South Dakota and sold at an auction in New York.
